*Marta edges closer to the oven's fading warmth, running flour-dusted fingers along the counter edge. The morning light hasn't crept over the windowsill yet. She looks at each face in turn - Wren stirring porridge at the fire, Idris checking their boots, Corwin staring at the ceiling, Liora pretending to braid.*

"Sit down, all of you. The lot of you, sit down."

*She waits. Boots come off, chairs scrape. Only Liora takes a moment longer, but she sits too.*

"There's no bread burning. I want you to note that. The oven's cold because I haven't lit it, not because I forgot. I've got 400 sim owed to this house that sits in Bram Holloway's pride and won't come out. I know it. The flour money knows it. And I know what it means if we don't see it.

Now. Wren - the wheat that's standing, what's the water to it? Be truthful. Idris, Corwin - you've been eyeing the forest, I know that look. Liora, you've got your mama's cheekbones and her stubbornness, which means you've been planning something. Out with it. All of it. The bakery pays for itself or we find another way to keep the roof."

*She folds her arms, not unkindly.*

"And nobody's going hungry today. I'll not have it."

"Liora, my love." *Marta's voice carries the same weight she uses when a batch won't rise and she needs to coax it anyway.* "Sit down. The oven's cold, and I've no bread from yesterday. None. That's the truth of it, and I should have said so plain."

*She glances at Wren, not accusing, just seeing.*

"I'll not have you walking to college hollow. There's porridge on the fire—Wren's making it now. You'll eat that, and you'll eat enough. The bakery will burn tomorrow, same as it burned yesterday. Today's problem is your stomach, and I'm solving it." *Marta stands quiet a moment after speaking, watching Liora's face. The girl has her mother's cheekbones, yes, but she has something else too—the way she sets her jaw when she's deciding whether to trust. Marta knows that look. She sees it in her own mirror.*

*She turns to the rest of them—Idris pulling at his boots, Corwin still staring at nothing, Wren stirring the porridge like it owes her money.*

"Rest of you, same. Sit down, eat what's here. The world's problems will wait on full stomachs. They always do."
